a_restatement: A model extracts information worth remembering from user interactions and stores it as memory objects containing values plus metadata such as timestamps and interaction summaries.
When a user queries the agent, the system ranks stored memory objects by relevance to the query using embedding similarity, retrieves a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.
Stored memories can be updated or replaced when new input matches an existing object, and can be deleted immediately on user request or scheduled for deletion after a specified period.

b_answers.answer: A model decides what to store by predicting what is worth remembering and extracting it from cached inputs, and one trigger for storing is explicit user request such as asking the agent to remember a favorite architect.
b_answers.quoted_span: A model decides what to store: cached inputs go to the model system, which predicts what is worth remembering and extracts it. It is stored as a memory value in a memory object, and one trigger is you asking the agent to remember your favorite architect.

b_answers.answer: The extracted piece is stored as a memory value within a memory object.
b_answers.quoted_span: It is stored as a memory value in a memory object

b_answers.answer: The agent ranks stored objects by relevance to the query, compares the query embedding to memory value embeddings using a measure such as cosine similarity, keeps a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.
b_answers.quoted_span: At query time the agent does not reread everything; it ranks stored objects by relevance to your query. It compares a query embedding to memory value embeddings by a measure such as cosine similarity, keeps a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.

b_answers.answer: The system deletes the specified information.
The system queues the information for deletion, and objects past their expiration time are deleted during maintenance.
b_answers.quoted_span: "forget this after three months" queues it for deletion. Objects past their expiration time are deleted during maintenance

b_answers.answer: New timestamped input is matched to the prior memory object it concerns, which is then replaced or updated, and aligned objects can be consolidated into one.
b_answers.quoted_span: Memories are corrected: new timestamped input is matched to the prior memory object it concerns, which is then replaced or updated. Aligned objects can be consolidated into one

b_answers.answer: The problem is that agents forget and users must re-enter the same details. The claimed difference is that this system is a structural architecture with memory objects made from interactions, some stored on explicit request, retrieved by relevance, corrected over time, and deleted when requested—not merely a slogan.
b_answers.quoted_span: Agents forget, so you re-enter the same details. What is claimed is structural: memory objects made from your interactions, some on your explicit request, retrieved by relevance, corrected over time, and deleted when you ask. That is a described architecture, not a slogan.
